title: StPR: Spatiotemporal Preservation and Routing for Exemplar-Free Video Class-Incremental Learning
one_liner: StPR learns new video action classes over time without storing old examples by preserving stable frame-level semantics and routing time patterns through specialized experts.
lead: Video class-incremental learning asks a model to learn new action categories one stage at a time without forgetting older ones. That is harder for video than for still images because the model must preserve both frame-level meaning and the way motion unfolds across time. This paper proposes StPR, an exemplar-free method that avoids storing old videos. It preserves stable frame semantics through selective distillation and routes different motion patterns through specialized experts, so the model can add new classes while keeping previously learned knowledge because old frame meaning is protected while new motion patterns get their own processing paths.

problem.h2: Continual video learning forgets both appearance and motion
paras: In class-incremental learning, new classes arrive in stages. After learning the next stage, the model should still recognize classes learned earlier. Many methods fight forgetting by storing old examples and replaying them during training, but that consumes memory and can create privacy problems.

Video adds another layer of difficulty. The model must remember not only what a frame contains, but also how the action changes over time. A method copied from image learning may preserve frame appearance while still forgetting the motion pattern that distinguishes one action from another.

callout.html: A video learner must preserve stable frame semantics and temporal structure at the same time, without replaying old videos.

panels.title: 1. Old action classes learned
panels.caption: The model already knows earlier actions from previous stages.

panels.title: 2. New classes arrive
panels.caption: Training on new actions can erase old ones if nothing is preserved.

panels.title: 3. Preserve stable frame semantics
panels.caption: The method locks onto the channels that still carry important frame meaning from earlier stages.

panels.title: 4. Route motion patterns to experts
panels.caption: Different time patterns are sent through different experts.

panels.title: 5. Learn new classes without replay
panels.caption: The model adds new actions while retaining earlier ones, even without stored old videos.

steps.text: Identify the channels whose frame-level meaning remains important for earlier classes.
Use selective distillation so those important channels do not drift too far when new classes are learned.
Split temporal behavior into components that can be handled by different experts.
Let a routing module choose which experts should process the current video's motion pattern.

steps.b: Predict without task IDs or replay
steps.text: At test time, the system recognizes all learned classes directly, without needing stored old examples or stage labels.

paras: The paper changes what gets preserved during continual learning. Instead of trying to freeze whole model blocks, it preserves only the frame-semantics channels that matter most and lets specialized temporal experts handle changing motion patterns.

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: stable semantic channels
hidden.name: which channels carry reusable frame meaning across learning stages
paras: Not every internal channel is equally important for retaining old knowledge. Some channels carry stable frame semantics that remain useful even when new classes arrive. Others can change more freely. StPR tries to find the stable set so it can preserve what truly matters instead of overconstraining the whole model.

The paper estimates this hidden set by combining channel sensitivity with class contribution. If changing a channel strongly harms earlier predictions and that channel contributes a lot to earlier classes, it should be preserved. This selective preservation helps because it protects old knowledge while still leaving room for adaptation.

heat.caption: Darker channels are more important to preserve because they carry stable frame semantics from earlier stages.

reads.html: These are the internal channels the model should protect if it wants to remember old actions.
Frame-Shared Semantics Distillation selects channels using sensitivity and classification contribution so that stable semantic information is preserved across increments.

mechanism.h2: Why selective preservation plus temporal routing reduces forgetting
paras: The first part of StPR protects earlier knowledge where it is most concentrated. Instead of freezing broad parts of the model, it preserves the channels that still matter for earlier classes. That is more flexible because unimportant channels remain free to adapt to new classes.

The second part handles time structure explicitly. Different actions share frame content yet differ in how motion evolves. By routing temporal patterns through specialized experts, the model can represent several kinds of motion behavior without forcing one shared pathway to absorb everything. This reduces interference between old and new actions because different temporal structures can use different experts.

Together, these two pieces solve complementary problems. Selective preservation keeps old frame semantics alive, and temporal routing gives the model enough specialized motion capacity to learn new actions without overwriting the old ones.

stages.s: route time patterns to specialized experts
learn new actions while retaining old ones

math.words: Give each channel a preservation score by combining how sensitive old predictions are to that channel with how much that channel contributes to old classes.
symbols: how much earlier predictions change when channel c changes
how strongly channel c supports earlier classes

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose channel 5 changes older predictions a lot, so sensitivity = 0.8.
Suppose channel 5 also contributes strongly to earlier classes, so contribution = 0.9.
A channel with sensitivity 0.2 and contribution 0.3 would get 0.06 and would be much less protected.
This selective rule helps because it preserves what matters most while leaving low-value channels free to adapt.

math.note: The exact paper machinery is richer, but the central idea is to preserve channels only when they are both important and vulnerable.

charts.title: Image-style or replay-free baseline
charts.note: Baselines often learn the new stage but forget older actions because they do not preserve time structure carefully enough.

charts.title: StPR
charts.note: Selective preservation plus temporal routing improves retention because frame semantics and motion patterns are both handled explicitly.

items.html: If the channel-selection signal is noisy, the method may protect the wrong channels and leave truly important old knowledge exposed.

items.b: Routing collapses to a few experts.
items.html: If most videos are sent through the same temporal experts, the model loses specialization and interference can return.

items.b: Large domain shift in video style.
items.html: If later stages look very different from earlier ones, preserving old semantics becomes harder because even high-value channels may need strong adaptation.
When stable channels are identified well and routing remains diverse, StPR reduces forgetting because it protects earlier frame meaning while giving new motion patterns their own processing paths.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Train a video classifier in several stages on disjoint action-class groups. Compare three settings: a replay-free baseline, a replay-based baseline, and StPR. After every stage, test on all classes learned so far and measure both old-class retention and new-class accuracy, while also verifying that prediction works without knowing the stage label at test time.
demo.closing: The demo should show that StPR preserves old actions without replay because it protects stable frame channels and routes motion patterns through specialized experts.
